title: I Used the Library Hold Policy on the Person Who Hid the Book

parts.text: I got a hold-ready email for a novel I had waited eleven weeks on. At the library the shelf was empty. A man two aisles over had the book spine-in on a cart he called his office. I was thirty-three. The hold policy said ready items stay on the hold shelf, not on private carts. I asked a librarian. She pulled it, scanned my card, and reminded him that offices are for staff. He said he was a researcher. Researchers still get in line. I read the first chapter on a bench that smelled like raincoats. Eleven weeks ended in ten minutes of policy. Spine-in is not a checkout. I turned a page. The cart went back to being a cart.

social.video_title: Eleven weeks, a spine-in cart, a hold that still had my name — Part 1/1
social.description: Empty hold shelf, researcher cart, raincoats. Would you have grabbed it off his pile yourself?
